when: Load when a task creates or edits an env.schema.ts, calls createEnv, documentEnv or validateEnv, or generates env-cap manifests, docs or reports. Skip it for other environment work.
purpose: env-cap gives each capability (a feature, service or package) its own environment contract: declared once as a static schema, validated at startup, and documented and aggregated at build time.
notFor: loading .env files, storing secrets, or a single global env object.
rules: Write each schema as a static literal in the module that owns it: schemas are parsed as source, never executed, so spreads, factories and re-exports are not understood.
Put `description`, `owner`, `expiresAt` and `category` in `documentEnv`. `createEnv` entries take `default`, `processor`, `validator`, `context`; its options `name` and `source: import.meta.url`.
Read a value through its owning contract (`paymentsEnv.STRIPE_KEY`). Never build a merged env object.
Call `validateEnv` once at startup, directly. Run the `generate*` functions only in a build script or CI.
Import only from package.json exports; `/build`, `/node` and `/eslint-plugin` are Node-only, never in browser code.
behavior: Reading a contract before `validateEnv` has run throws `EnvNotReadyError`.
Errors never contain values. Keep raw values out of your own processor and validator messages, and do not spread a contract.
`required: true` in `documentEnv` only documents a variable as required. Enforcement is the validator rejecting an empty value.
`context` is a plain string your application activates, not a security boundary.

Two contracts may declare one variable name. Conflicting processor return types and exclusive-group violations are errors; differing processor or validator sources warn, and block under `onIncompatibility: "throw"`.

mistakes.wrong: `createEnv({ ...base })`, or a schema built by a function
mistakes.right: Declare the schema as a literal object in the module that owns it, then pass that one binding to `createEnv` and `documentEnv`.
Keep a static `expiresAt`; pass `liveExpirationDates` to the generator.

verify: Run the project's type check and tests.
After changing an `env.schema.ts`, update its `documentEnv()` entry and run `generate:env`. Commit generated files only if the project does; never hand-edit one.

references.when: Every option of the generators and the CLI
Moving off dotenv, raw process.env, Zod, envalid or t3-env

imports.@maverickcer/env-cap/build: Node only: discovery, analysis and generating the manifest, docs and reports
imports.@maverickcer/env-cap/node: Node only: `nodeBuildFileSystem`, the file system a build script hands to `/build`
imports.@maverickcer/env-cap/evidence: `defineEvidenceProjection`, pure transforms over the evidence model
imports.@maverickcer/env-cap/eslint-plugin: Node only: the `no-raw-process-env` and `no-node-fs` lint rules
